pages.text: Analytic continuation: a function known near one point is carried to another a disc at a time, re-expanding its series in each. In a disc of radius ρ, cutting the series after N terms leaves about (ρ/R)^(N+1), where R is how far the series converges. Covering a distance L takes L/ρ discs.
$(thing)Set$(): Disc radius, Terms.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): A rough function: its radius of convergence varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The disc reaches past the radius of convergence: the series diverges.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Less summing is faster.
